intent: Change only the mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg, to reduce yaw inertia, following the Integrator's conditional trigger. Keep the five sensors at x = ±0.024 m, y = 0.06 m, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.12 m track, the 0.03 m wheels and the body unchanged. I expect slalom progress above 0.2, slalom max_error at or below 0.06 m, and oval oscillation below about 0.15. I expect the s-bend to hold its current completion. Considering but not committing: a wider spread (±0.032 m) if the slalom line losses rise above 2 per run after the mass change, and a body change only if off-track limits become the constraint, which the current geometry does not show.
learning: Hypotheses for this race: (1) at 0.6 kg, slalom max_error falls to 0.06 m or below and slalom progress rises above 0.2; (2) oval steering oscillation falls below about 0.15; (3) s-bend completion holds at or above 0.3 with line losses at or below 2 per run. If (1) and (2) hold, the yaw-inertia lever is confirmed and I will keep 0.6 kg. If the slalom still fails with lower oscillation, the limit is likely sensing reach on the reversal, and I will consider the ±0.032 m spread. If the s-bend falls back, I will revert toward 0.8 kg and test a smaller spread instead.
rationale: Iteration 2 is the best result so far (score 501.2, up from 166.4). The oval now finishes 20 of 20 runs. The s-bend finishes 6 of 20, and the slalom still finishes 0 of 20. Both failing tracks end off track. Line-loss events are 0.9 on the s-bend and 1.0 on the slalom, well below the 2-per-run threshold, so the sensor spread of ±0.024 m is not failing and I am not widening it. Max error on the s-bend is now 0.0529 m, under the 0.06 m limit, so the s-bend is no longer clearly stuck at the limit. The slalom max error is 0.0628 m, above the limit, and its progress is only 0.10. Oval steering oscillation is 0.206, above the roughly 0.15 level the Integrator flagged. Integration feedback asked me to try a lower mass (about 0.6 kg) if oscillation stays high and s-bend and slalom still hit max_error near 0.06 m with progress below 0.25. That condition is met on the slalom (max_error 0.063, progress 0.10, oscillation high on the oval) but not on the s-bend, where progress is 0.85. I am taking the mass step because the slalom is the binding failure and the yaw-inertia reduction is the only geometry lever the Integrator named. I am changing only the mass, from 0.8 to 0.6 kg. The sensors, body, track, wheels and sensor size stay as they were, so the effect of the mass change is isolated from the Integrator's controller change as far as one race allows. Body width still sets the off-track limit at its 0.06 m floor, so I am not touching it. I expect slalom progress to rise above 0.2 and max error to fall toward or below 0.06 m, with oval oscillation dropping below about 0.15. I expect the s-bend to hold near its current completion rate. I am not sure of this, because the Integrator's controller also changes in this iteration.
